snp5.19:0.2: (Verses on the Recital of the Way to the Beyond)
snp5.19:1.1: “I will recite the Way to the Beyond, said venerable Piṅgiya,
snp5.19:1.4: as he saw it, so he explained: unstained, with great intelligence,
snp5.19:1.5: the one free from sense desire, the unentangled one, the Strong One, why should he speak falsely?
snp5.19:2.2: Of the one who gave up stain and delusion, who gave up conceit and malevolence,
snp5.19:2.3: come now, I will proclaim this lyric which is endowed with beauty:
snp5.19:3.1: The Buddha, the darkness-dispeller, the All-Seeing Visionary,
snp5.19:3.2: who has gone to the end of the world, transcended all of existence
snp5.19:3.3: given up all suffering, the one pollutant-free,
snp5.19:3.4: whose very name is truth - O brahmin, (you are) worshipped by me.
snp5.19:4.1: Just as a bird who has given up a barren woodland,
snp5.19:4.2: might live in a forest which has much fruit,
snp5.19:4.3: so too I have given up those of little wisdom,
snp5.19:4.4: like a swan who has arrived at the great sea.
snp5.19:5.1: Those who explained (things) to me in the past, before Gotama’s teaching,
snp5.19:5.3: saying ‘it was so, and so it will be’, all that was just hearsay,
snp5.19:5.5: all that just increased my thoughts.
snp5.19:6.2: Alone sits the Darkness-Dispeller, the Bright One, the Light-Maker,
snp5.19:6.3: Gotama of Great Knowledge, Gotama of Great Intelligence.
snp5.19:7.2: He who taught the Teaching to me, which is visible, not subject to time,
snp5.19:7.4: the end of craving, beyond calamity, for which there is nowhere a likeness.”
snp5.19:8.1: [Bāvari:] “Then why do you dwell apart from him, even for a second, Piṅgiya,
snp5.19:8.3: from Gotama of Great Knowledge, Gotama of Great Intelligence,
snp5.19:9.2: he who taught the Teaching to you, which is visible, not subject to time,
snp5.19:9.4: the end of craving, beyond calamity, for which there is nowhere a likeness?”
snp5.19:10.1: “I would not dwell apart from him even for a second, brahmin,
snp5.19:10.3: from Gotama of Great Knowledge, Gotama of Great Intelligence,
snp5.19:11.2: he who taught the Teaching to me, which is visible, not subject to time,
snp5.19:11.4: the end of craving, beyond calamity, for which there is nowhere a likeness.
snp5.19:12.1: I see him in my mind as though with the eye,
snp5.19:12.2: (as I dwell) heedful night and day, brahmin.
snp5.19:12.3: revering him I make the night pass by,
snp5.19:12.4: for that reason I think there is no (real) dwelling apart.
snp5.19:13.1: My confidence, happiness, mind, and mindfulness,
snp5.19:13.2: do not depart from Gotama’s teaching,
snp5.19:13.3: whatever direction the One of Great Wisdom goes to
snp5.19:13.4: it is that very place that I am inclined.
snp5.19:14.1: I am old, without strength and feeble,
snp5.19:14.2: because of that my body does not go there,
snp5.19:14.3: but by an effort of thought I always go,
snp5.19:14.4: for my mind, Brahmin, is joined to him.
snp5.19:15.1: Lying down in a quagmire I was trembling,
snp5.19:15.2: I drifted from island to island,
snp5.19:15.3: then I saw the Sambuddha, the flood-crosser, the one pollutant-free.”
snp5.19:16.1: [The Buddha:] “Just as Vakkali released his confidence -
snp5.19:16.3: just like that you must release your confidence,
snp5.19:16.4: and you will go, Piṅgiya, beyond the realm of Death.”
snp5.19:17.1: “I am more and more sure about this, having heard the sage’s word,
snp5.19:17.3: the cover-remover, the Sambuddha, who is unhindered, assured in speech,
snp5.19:18.1: who knows the great gods, who has understood everything far and near,
snp5.19:18.3: the Teacher who makes an end to questions in those who have doubts, and make them known.
snp5.19:19.2: The Indestructible, the Unagitated, for which there is nowhere a likeness,
snp5.19:19.3: Surely I will go there, about this I have no doubt,
snp5.19:19.4: thus bear me in mind as one whose heart is intent (on Nibbāna).”
